title: Getting started with flowcam
text: find_cameras() returns tibble camera metadata. arguments fetches available cameras; pass site_id narrow results specific NWIS site. Pecos Web Camera near Roswell, NM (NWIS site 08385630) well-known site Pecos River: Key columns returned: already know camera ID, look directly: limit network traffic need fields, use return_fields:

text: list_images() returns filenames stored camera. Filenames alone enough build download URLs via build_image_url(). default result single-column tibble filenames. Set raw_item = TRUE also retrieve timestamps file sizes: Pass POSIXct values (UTC) fetch images specific window:
code: cam_id <- cam$camId[[1]]  # 10 most recent images imgs <- list_images(cam_id, limit = 10) imgs list_images(cam_id, limit = 10, raw_item = TRUE) list_images(   cam_id,   after  = as.POSIXct("2025-06-01 00:00:00", tz = "UTC"),   before = as.POSIXct("2025-06-02 00:00:00", tz = "UTC") )

title: Getting started with flowcam
text: build_image_url() combines camera’s base S3 directory filenames returned list_images(): size argument controls image dimensions: "small" (default) — ~720 px wide, suitable monitoring dashboards "overlay" — full-size overlay image gage-reading annotation "thumb" — thumbnail ~200 px tall
code: urls <- build_image_url(cam, imgs$filename, size = "small") head(urls)

what: Fetching recent images at the Roswell camera
title: Monitoring the Pecos River with flowcam and dataRetrieval
text: Retrieve 20 recent images metadata know timestamps: timestamp NIMS YYYY-MM-DDTHH-MM-SSZ format records image capture time UTC. fs column gives file size kilobytes.
code: cam_id <- roswell$camId[[1]]  recent <- list_images(cam_id, limit = 20, raw_item = TRUE) recent

title: Monitoring the Pecos River with flowcam and dataRetrieval
text: Retrieve mean daily discharge (parameter code 00060) downstream Acme gage (08386000) period. NWIS data easy pull dataRetrieval::readNWISdv():
code: # Derive date range from the images we just listed # timestamps are like "2025-06-15T14-30-00Z" ts_clean <- gsub("T(\\d{2})-(\\d{2})-(\\d{2})Z$", "T\\1:\\2:\\3Z",                   recent$timestamp) image_times <- as.POSIXct(ts_clean, format = "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", tz = "UTC")  start_date <- format(min(image_times), "%Y-%m-%d") end_date   <- format(max(image_times), "%Y-%m-%d")  flow <- readNWISdv(   siteNumbers = "08386000",   parameterCd = "00060",   startDate   = start_date,   endDate     = end_date ) flow <- renameNWISColumns(flow) flow

what: Downloading images around a flow event
title: Monitoring the Pecos River with flowcam and dataRetrieval
text: Suppose Acme gage recorded notable rise. Download images Roswell camera bracketing period see whether visible upstream: Re-running download_images() partial download safe: files already dest skipped unless pass overwrite = TRUE.
code: event_start <- as.POSIXct("2025-06-10 00:00:00", tz = "UTC") event_end   <- as.POSIXct("2025-06-12 23:59:59", tz = "UTC")  dest <- file.path(tempdir(), "pecos_event") dir.create(dest, showWarnings = FALSE)  paths <- download_images(   cam_id   = cam_id,   dest_dir = dest,   size     = "small",   after    = event_start,   before   = event_end,   limit    = 50 )  # How many images were captured during the event window? length(paths)

title: Monitoring the Pecos River with flowcam and dataRetrieval

code: # Build URLs for the overlay version of the same images imgs <- list_images(cam_id,                     after  = event_start,                     before = event_end,                     limit  = 5)  overlay_urls <- build_image_url(roswell, imgs$filename, size = "overlay") overlay_urls

title: Monitoring the Pecos River with flowcam and dataRetrieval
text: Acme gage (08386000) ~45 km downstream Roswell camera (08385630). Checking cameras day makes possible track flood wave moving reach:
code: # List the most recent image from each site on the same day roswell_imgs <- list_images(roswell$camId[[1]], limit = 1, raw_item = TRUE) acme_imgs    <- list_images(acme$camId[[1]],   limit = 1, raw_item = TRUE)  rbind(   data.frame(site = "Roswell (08385630)", roswell_imgs),   data.frame(site = "Acme (08386000)",    acme_imgs) )

title: Monitoring the Pecos River with flowcam and dataRetrieval
text: Rate limits: unauthenticated requests share pool across users. Call set_nims_key() (see vignette("getting-started")) raise personal limit. Large downloads: set limit conservatively exploring; images "small" size roughly 150–300 KB . "thumb" size useful need visual overview. Time zones: NIMS timestamps UTC. tz column camera metadata records local time zone installation need convert. Image availability: newestImageDT camera metadata gives age recent image—useful detecting outages start download loop.
